lens_summary.drift: m9-67 is a single-commit B-direct cycle that adds a smoke test for the most failure-prone vault drift CCs. The test was developed and validated locally: 4 tests, 0 failures, ~35s wall time. The test uses git clone --shared (not git archive) because many python CCs call git log via subprocess and need a working .git. The script avoids trap-based cleanup because subshell command substitution would inherit the trap and clean up prematurely — cleanup is explicit at script exit.

subject.fix: Added scripts/smoke_test_ccs.sh that clones the repo into a /tmp work dir, injects synthetic drift into CC#4 (wrong SHA in archive-manifest), CC#39 (wrong Total cycles in cycles/index.md), CC#46 (fake fix/m9-99-smoke-test branch), and verifies the CC#48+CC#54 meta-checks pass on clean state. Each test asserts exit code and DRIFT line. Cost: ~35 seconds.
subject.gap: m9-65 discovered 49 stale branches because CC#46 only matched fix/m9-* (missing chore/*, feat/mX-*, ms-*). m9-66 discovered 54 stale SHAs because CC#4 had a broken awk regex. Both drifted silently for many cycles. No automated test exercises the CC detection chain end-to-end.

legacy_findings_preserved.summary: No automated mechanism to catch silent failures of critical vault drift CCs. m9-65 and m9-66 each discovered drift that had been accumulating silently for many cycles. Added scripts/smoke_test_ccs.sh to inject synthetic drift and verify the meta-check chain still catches it.
